question:
Using the inverse-matrix method, solve
$$x+y+z=6$$
$$y+2z=8$$
$$2x+z=5$$

(a) Form the matrices $A$, $X$, and $B$, and establish that $A^{-1}$ exists.

(b) Find $A^{-1}$ using the adjoint method and hence determine $x$, $y$, and $z$.

(c) Verify the solution in the given equations.
explanation:
(a)
The system can be written as $AX=B$, where
$$A=\begin{bmatrix}1 & 1 & 1\\0 & 1 & 2\\2 & 0 & 1\end{bmatrix},\quad X=\begin{bmatrix}x\\y\\z\end{bmatrix},\quad B=\begin{bmatrix}6\\8\\5\end{bmatrix}$$
Expanding the determinant,
$$|A|=1\begin{vmatrix}1 & 2\\0 & 1\end{vmatrix}-1\begin{vmatrix}0 & 2\\2 & 1\end{vmatrix}+1\begin{vmatrix}0 & 1\\2 & 0\end{vmatrix}$$
$$|A|=1-(-4)-2=3\neq0$$
Therefore, $A^{-1}$ exists.

(b)
The adjoint of $A$ is
$$\operatorname{adj}A=\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 1\\4 & -1 & -2\\-2 & 2 & 1\end{bmatrix}$$
Therefore,
$$A^{-1}=\frac{1}{3}\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 1\\4 & -1 & -2\\-2 & 2 & 1\end{bmatrix}$$
Now,
$$X=A^{-1}B$$
$$X=\frac{1}{3}\begin{bmatrix}1 & -1 & 1\\4 & -1 & -2\\-2 & 2 & 1\end{bmatrix}\begin{bmatrix}6\\8\\5\end{bmatrix}$$
$$X=\frac{1}{3}\begin{bmatrix}6-8+5\\24-8-10\\-12+16+5\end{bmatrix}=\frac{1}{3}\begin{bmatrix}3\\6\\9\end{bmatrix}$$
Hence,
$$x=1,\quad y=2,\quad z=3$$

(c)
$$1+2+3=6$$
$$2+2(3)=8$$
$$2(1)+3=5$$
Thus, the solution is verified.

options.C:
(a) $|A|=0$, so $A^{-1}$ does not exist
(b) The system has infinitely many solutions
(c) $(1,2,3)$ is one possible solution
